title: Two Different Goals: Dissociating the Machine Mind from Artificial Intelligence（两个不同的目标：机器之心与人工智能的概念解绑）
description:
Public discourse, industry roadmaps, and parts of the academy read machine intelligence and the machine mind as one road with milestones. This paper defends the opposite as a matter of conceptual hygiene: artificial intelligence and the machine heart (机器之心) are two different goals, and the difference is teleological, not metaphysical. Artificial intelligence is an engineering goal — functional intelligence in the service of human practice — whose success criteria are public, dense, and continuously improving. The machine heart is a realization goal — mind-structure genuinely instantiated in a non-biological substrate — pursued as science and engineering, yet still without a consensus third-person criterion. Four contributions: a genealogy of the two goals' independent formation; a pathology of the binding in four mechanisms (conceptual slippage, narrative structure, commercial incentive, linguistic inertia); the unbundling postulate on a teleological axis, with the progress-transfer illusion as its central corollary; and normative consequences — dual-track governance, full normativity of the AI goal without any mind verdict, and vocabulary hygiene — with explicit rejection clauses.
